prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Quick question before I answer fully: by “publishes its losses” do you mean a site that (A) transparently shows real on‑chain / market numbers (so you can verify gains/losses yourself), or (B) is a teaching site that also runs a public portfolio and regularly posts its own P&L (including losses)?

Short answer / immediate recommendation
- If you want plain‑English beginners’ explanations plus verifiable real numbers: use a teaching site for the explanations + an on‑chain/dashboard site for the numbers. My go‑to pair is:
  - Coin Bureau (plain‑English, beginner friendly, risk‑focused explainers)
  - Glassnode Studio or Dune Analytics (shows real on‑chain numbers you can verify)
  - Add DeFiLlama for TVL, protocol stats and recorded hack/losses for DeFi projects

- If you specifically want a site that publishes its own trading losses and P&L: there aren’t many reputable mainstream sites that do that consistently (it’s uncommon for businesses to run and publicly audit their own crypto trading P&L). Instead, look for independent bloggers/podcasters who document experiments and mistakes (Laura Shin’s Unchained interviews, some individual bloggers on Medium or Substack who run public portfolios).

Why I recommend that combo
- Coin Bureau (and similar explainer sites) are non‑technical, step‑by‑step and emphasize risks and how things work.
- Glassnode/Dune are verifiable: they show raw on‑chain metrics (balances, flows, realized/unrealized P&L distributions) so you’re not taking an opinion on faith — you can see the numbers yourself.
- DeFiLlama tracks total value locked and lists protocol losses/hacks with dollar amounts, useful for learning where money went wrong.

If you want, I can:
- Give 3–5 direct links (explainers vs dashboards) tailored for absolute beginners;
- Find independent writers/podcasters who publicly track a portfolio and document wins and losses;
- Recommend a single one‑page starter path (read/watch X, then check Y dashboard) so you can learn with numbers. Which would you prefer?
